heading: Preamble
text: Each morning a new star, new life. Ships adrift in the cosmos. The wayfarers whispered life into each corner, blessing them with a sip from their chalice. When they found our shores, it would be the last stop on their journey. Their ship was knocked from the sky by the great belt circling the planet. Their people tried to rebuild and tried to leave, but the planet kept them here. Striking their rafts and their boats with hot iron from those rings. Among them, the one who carried the chalice spilled their cup, the cosmos filling the land in deep rivers. Those who drank of the banks of the starlit river became more, felt more, and knew more. These would be our ancestors, the first of the Consecrated; the ones who would build the cornerstones of our society.

heading: Stamina
text: To play the game you will need a series of D8 dice, these will represent your stamina as a character. Starting out, you will begin with an amount equivalent to 5 + Body Stat. To utilize stamina, you choose a skill or action, and roll a number of dice according to the skill or predetermined by the GM. This represents the effort exerted to complete an action. Some actions are more complicated and may require more dice. Rolling 8’s represent strain, and will cause you to temporarily lose a stamina dice until you rest or recover. For example, to utilize a certain skill you must utilize 3 dice, if any of the dice rolled are an eight, you lose a die from your stamina pool.

heading: Recovery & Resting
text: Your ability to recover depends on the amount of time you rest, as well as your Grit Stat. There are a few types of rest, Breathers, Rest, & Recovery. Breathers Rest Recovery Generally understood as less than three hours but as short as thirty minutes. Breathers represent you treating any minor wounds, recovering from some conditions and other related activities. Generally understood as taking an entire evening and some hours to sleep, rest and recoup. Usually a minimum of seven hours, a maximum of twelve hours. Generally understood as taking several days to completely recover, typically a week. This is more involved and usually allows you to recover from multiple injuries and treat various conditions. This is the only way to heal major injuries without outside intervention. Recoup Stamina Equal to your Grit Stat Remove One Minor Condition or Injury Recoup All Stamina Remove injuries or conditions with combined magnitude of up to 2 + ½ Grit rounding up, Cannot heal Major Injuries. Recoup All Stamina Remove All Minor and Moderate Injuries. Remove A Number of Major Injuries equivalent to your grit stat.

heading: Bidding
text: Behind every basic mechanic and at the heart of the game is the bidding system. In that across the board all dice rolls are essentially the same. You will utilize your dice pool (your Stamina) and determine the number of dice you are willing to while risk completing an action. Your maximum stamina is equivalent to your Body Stat + 5. You do have a limiter on how many die you are allowed to spend on any one action/bid at a time. This is called Exertion and is determined by your Soul stat which is gone over later. This doesn’t include any bonuses from feats or other things. The action of rolling your die is called bidding. This can be moving in combat, attacking, casting a spell, tinkering on a machine, etc. Any action that uses some modicum of skill will require bidding, especially early on. Think about bidding as effort put into an action. Actions you excel at will require lower effort, and those that you aren’t as skill at will require more effort. You are effectively choosing how many dice you want to use and rolling said dice. The die roll is to see if you incur any strain from your efforts, meaning rolling an 8 means you are strained while performing an action and loose one stamina per 8 from your pool until you manage to rest. Rolling multiple eights can result in a complication in completing an action, and in certain cases, failure. Complications generally are narrative, but on occasion can affect the outcome of a check in unexpected ways. Rolling 1 or multiple 1’s represents your character having focus, clarity or a certain amount of luck. Each one allows you to add +1 to an effect, or allow you a small advantage during story, clearing minor conditions, gaining social leverage. This will largely be determined by the scenario and your GM. Any roll between 2-7 on a die represents a good effort on your character's part and doesn’t overly affect success or failure of a roll. Loosing all of your stamina leaves your character Fatigued and generally unable to take actions without risk to themselves. Certain abilities let you push past this limit. With that in mind you aren’t rolling to hit a number, but rather to see how your energy is spent. The only goal is to bid higher than the effort, or guard required by the opposing force. Furthermore, you will not know how many dice you need to roll to win a bid unless you have a special feat that allows you to know such information. For example: Essentially say you are trying to pick a lock, Make your bid, (choose how much effort to expend, or how many die from your stamina pool you will risk) The action has a hidden challenge rating which is equivalent to a number of dice which your GM knows. You will roll your dice to see if you incur any strain from your action. You bid 5 die, and have a bonus of 1 from a feat, so a total of six die. This is over the difficulty known only by the GM( in this case it was 3) which means you are successful in your action. However, you rolled an eight, which means you lose stamina until your next rest. Roll Effect Multiple 8s X Strain + Story Complication: Any event which can affect you or your party narratively in a negative fashion. 8 1 Strain Per 8 Rolled 2-7 No effect/Normal Effort 1 1 Story Opportunity: Any event or opportunity granted to you or your party for actions carried out with great skill and finesse. Effort Pooling - Assistance At any point you can choose to act as a group rather than an individual when it comes to completing tasks. This is usually on a case by case basis where it makes sense narratively - but you can choose to assist others by allowing them to utilize any number of dice from your stamina pool. These dice are considered used and subtracted from your pool until rest. There is a risk in this that any strain accumulated by the primary party affects anybody that assisted as well in addition to assistance dice. You can choose to assist in combat to guard or otherwise if you have reasonable opportunity.

heading: Primary Stats
text: Outside your stamina, other smaller aspects of your personhood and interactions with the world will be affected by the three primary stats gone over below. These may seem inconsequential, but they make up the core of your character. Each affects many things outside itself that might not be immediately obvious; these are gone over below and how each primary stat affects your secondary abilities. The total max for each stat is 12, with stats being upgraded by spending merit between sessions or at rest. The cost of buying a point depends on how many you already have in a stat. The table for these purchases is below.

heading: Mind
text: In totality, mind encompasses knowledge, awareness, reasoning, and other related things. It’s your ability to think through problems and also maintain your sense of self. Reputation : this is people's natural perception of you based on your actions in and around the world. In addition to sentiment, it can affect how certain interactions with different people will go. (= 1+ Mind / 2 Rounded Down) Scope : The number of spells you can know and have active at any time. (= 1 + Mind) Poise : your resistance to social magic and undue influence and how effective your social interactions are. (=1 + Mind / 2 Rounded Up)

heading: Body
text: This represents your character's physical form and capabilities. This includes your strength, speed, and reaction time. As well as resistance to certain maladies and effects. Stamina : How much energy you have to expend through a day before you need to rest. (5 + Body) Injury Slots : The amount of damage you can take before incapacitation or death. (2 + Body) Tempo : How fast you react and move through the world. (= 2 + Body / 2 Rounded Up)

heading: Soul
text: This is you, the force of your person. One could describe it as will, presence, ambition, and persistence. Soul helps keep your character grounded and themselves. It resists magic’s corruptions and helps you stay you. Grit : Directly affects your ability to recover during rest as well as recover from certain conditions over time. (= 1 + Soul / 2 Rounded Down) Stability : Determines your ability to resist the influence of magical corruption. (1 + Soul / 2 Rounded Up) Exertion : Determines the maximum amount of effort you can expend from your stamina on any single bid. (Soul + 2)

heading: Increasing Primary Stats
text: Throughout gameplay you will garner merit, through your deeds and actions, selling crafts, and other tasks. You will learn more about merit specifically later on. As you gather merit though, you can spend it to improve your gear, or in this case your self. The cost of Stat points (Mind, Body, Soul) is laid out along with the merit it costs to increase at each level below. Primary Stats Improvements Stat Level Merit Cost 1 3 2 6 3 9 4 12 5 15 6 18 7 21 8 24 9 27 10 30 11 33 12 36 For any buys above 12+ your GM should adjudicate whether it’s reasonable or not and what an appropriate cost should be. Currently all stats are tuned specifically to move between 0 - 12

heading: Stability
text: There is magic rife in this world, flowing between the creatures, the land, and the plants. It’s a mystery's balance and changes everything it touches. Occasionally these forces can warp and alter things in unexpected ways. Everyone has various levels of susceptibility to these changes; how people react to them is highly dependent on the culture. This could be an extra horn, a couple of years of age, hooves, hair, or even a change in eye color. Derived from your Soul stat. Your total Stability is equal to 1 + ½ your Soul stat, rounded up. You will use this when the situation calls for it; this will act as a bonus to any bid you make against resisting increasing corruption. To avoid corruption, you must bid for any number of actions, including, but not limited to: Repeated casting of a spell over a short duration Casting a powerful spell with multiple components Entering an area that has been corrupted or is out of magical balance Spending prolonged time with contaminated objects Encountering unusual creatures Getting hit by certain spells and abilities.

heading: Health - Injury Slots
text: Health is determined by your body start and is represented as Injury Slots. To determine your starting health, you will add your Body Stat +2. Each slot represents a degree of physical damage to your character, and some may come with specific effects/feats that affect other aspects of play. It is important to note that injuries are separate from stamina. If you fill all of your injury slots, your character reaches Fatigue automatically and is considered Incapacitated, and in some cases, could die.

heading: Injuries
text: Injuries are specified by you or your target usually. Where you hit, though, is more of a specific feat and skill you gain over time and training. The type of damage depends on the weapon or what caused the injury in the first place. Most all weapons do physical damage, while spells do elemental damage. Injuries vary in magnitude from 1 to 4, representing Mild, Moderate, Major and Fatal. Most injuries will be mild and moderate, with a rare few crossing the threshold into Major and Fatal. When adding an injury to your injury track, you will include the injury name, any notes, the body part affected, and any linked conditions. Each injury will show up as a card and describe what the injury is and its severity. In addition, injuries introduce penalties to your maximum stamina that lasts as long as you have the injury. Minor Moderate Major Fatal -1 Maximum Stamina -2 Maximum Stamina -3 Maximum Stamina No Stamina All minor injuries merely affect your stamina. These are usually superficial or injuries which will easily heal on their own. Imposes a narrative limit or condition Large impact on day-to-day life These injuries will almost always deliver a character to deaths door without serious and immediate intervention. Healing : breather, rest, recovery or basic care are usually enough to clear these conditions. Healing : requires rest and/or proper care. Healing : requires intensive care, sufficient time, or unique items to clear. Healing : Some spells, feats and other things can potentially bring something or someone back from the dead. Below is the table that lists several types of injuries, there is a chance a new or different injury will be imposed, however these instances can be decided by the GM. Injury Table Name Notes Frost Bite X At minimum nerve damage, at major lose of limbs or appendages. Burn X At minimum small blisters, at major large chunks of flesh to the bone damaged. Laceration X At minimum, small cuts, at major large gashes and open wounds. Abrasions X At minimum a scraped knee, at major large swathes of missing skin. Broken Bone X At the lowest level this is minor fracture, at a major level this could mean shattered bones. Internal Bleeding X At the lowest level this represents minor bruising, at the highest major internal bleeding. Organ Damage X Typically, not experienced at lower injury levels, this represents small punctures to full failure. Minor wounds might include injections, claws, and the like. Major might be major knife, spear or arrow wounds. This can also come from excessive or overuse of a muscle or body part. Hypothermia X A condition caused by exposure to low temperatures for extended periods of time without proper gear or heat. Incapacitated You have taken on more damage than you can stand, you are no longer able to take actions until you receive healing. *Death Complete cessation of life.

heading: On Death
text: Players should have an honest discussion before the game on their expectations of how things should work during gameplay. For the best possible outcome, the GM and players should agree on how serious or often deaths should occur. Things to consider should include, how deadly is combat and whether death is permenant or not. As is, the system has feats and abilities that can be included or excluded based on these discussions.

heading: Conditions
text: There are a wide number of conditions in the game that can afflict the player, party, or NPCs. You do not need to be familiar with all of them, but they are listed below for convenience’s sake. They can affect you in any type of scene across the entirety of gameplay. You may notice X’s next to some of these in a similar fashion as injuries, these represent magnitude, or severity. Condition Description Effect Resolves Duress X You feel threatened - there is an undercurrent of anxiety to everything you do. You take an additional 1 strain for each count of tax any time you would bid. You take an action to steady yourself, remove a counter of X. Unsteady Your stance is compromised somehow; it is harder to balance. You are unable to move unless you take an action to find your footing. Using a movement action to steady yourself. Exposed You lack proper protection in a scenario against an outside threat. For any bid against an environmental factor, you face increased difficulty to resist injury. This means that bids will incur a penalty until Exposed is resolved. Upon finding shelter, putting on protective gear or being prepared for specific environmental conditions. Fatigue You have utilized all of your energy. You need rest. You can continue to bid, but may only use up to 2 die to do so Rest. Immobilized Your movement has been limited. You are unable to move or make ranged attacks without first freeing yourself. You must take an action to bid to free yourself from what is holding you. Conspicuous You are unable to hide; people notice you and your every action. You are more readily targeted and noticed; you easily raise suspicion. You must make a bid to make yourself less conspicuous or hide. Concealed You are well disguised; others are unlikely to notice you. You can move and take actions without being noticed. Ends if you attack or draw attention to yourself. Slowed X Your movement has somehow been restricted. It is more difficult to move. Your Tempo is halved, rounded down for the duration. Condition clears after X turns or leaving an area. Stunned X The number of actions you can take next turn is reduced. Your action points are reduced by X during your next turn. After a turn has passed, this condition resolves. Impulsed You are compelled to take a specific action. The GM suggests an action; you may take it, or receive the Duress Condition. If you already are afflicted by duress and choose to resist the impulse, you take an additional magnitude of duress. After action is taken or Duress is applied. Quickened X You become faster, able to react quicker. You gain an additional action point to utilize during your next turn. Condition clears after the next turn. Fear X You become scared, and feel the urge to hide and run. You cannot move closer to the afflicter of this condition. Condition clears after X turns. Blinded X You are unable to see. Your Exertion is reduced by 2 for any action that requires sight. Condition clears after X turns Silenced X You cannot cast or use magic. You cannot use spells for the duration of this condition. Condition clears after X turns. Infected You have some kind of infection, bacterial, viral, or magical. Dependent on illness. After being treated or resting. Poisoned You are suffering the effects of a poison You suffer additional strain when rolling an 8. After treatment or rest. Embarrassed You feel a twinge of awkwardness from a social faux pas or other action. You cannot reroll social actions. After a positive interaction. Resentful You feel strong negative feelings towards another person or party. Harder to build rapport with others. Improve sentiment, or have higher leverage. Convivial You are more likely to believe and get along with others. The first social complication of each scene is softened. Reverent You are awed by someone and are unable to act against them. You cannot harm the person unless the stakes are high. The entity does something negative towards you. Suspicious You are deeply unsure of someone and their motives. It is easier to read motives but more difficult to build rapport. Fortified X You are steeled against any incoming attack or thing targeting you. Your guard for any bid to defend yourself is counted X higher instead. Spell ends or is dispelled. Vulnerable X You are in a weakened state. For each count of X, any bid to resist a damage type specified by the inflicter's choice during an opposing bid has an - X penalty. The condition or injury is applied, or the effect is dispelled. Starving X You haven’t consumed adequate nutrients, it has left you weakened. For each count of X, all bids you make are penalized by - X. You consume food or nutrients. Dehydration X You haven’t had fluid or water for an extended period. For each count of X, all bids you make are penalized by - X. You intake fluid. Sharpened X You feel an acute awareness for even the smallest details; not much will go without your notice. Any bid that requires your senses gains X bonus dice. The effect wears off. Dulled X You have something clouding your perception; you notice less. Any bid that requires your senses gains an - X penalty. The effect wears off.

text: Throughout the worlds, there are a number of disease of different types, which can affect your interactions with others and ability to do certain actions in the day to day. These are represented below and all have magnitudes similar to some conditions and injuries as you’ve become familiar with them. Disease Table Name Effects Iraventus (Rain Lung) Relatively common, transmitted via fluids. Causes coughing, body aches and dehydration. Fulgallis (Static) Relatively common, transmitted via contaminated surfaces. Causes debilitating rashes which have a specific branching pattern. Senius (Bastard’s Rot) A variety of necrotizing bacteria which enters soft tissue causing sores and possible necrotic patches. Vendespuo (VDP) Causes intense stomach pain, intestinal distress and high fever. Highly contagious. Amissen (Violist’s Bane) Transmitted via particulates in the air. A serious condition which attacks the nervous system. In minor severity, it causes numbness, while more serious cases can attack the brain and whole limb function. Gena A disease transmitted by insects of differing types. Causes profuse sweating, disorientation, and mild hallucinations at higher severity. Vox A unique disease that attacks the vocal cords and throat, can cause loss of voice temporarily or permanently. The conditions of which largely depend on the species of creature it was attained from. Generally the disease causes confusion, spontaneous amelioration, and irritability. Slipped Cuases the infected to somehow be dislodged from the normal flow of time, whether they experience it slower of faster than the average person is highly dependent on the case.

heading: Resistance
text: Resistance exists as a feat that is added to certain characters and players depending on the scenario. A resistance will take the form of: Resistance X. Where X represents a number of die. The type of resistance is mentioned by the feat. This means for each time a player guards against some attack, environmental factor, or social situation of the resistance type, a player's guard or bid is treated as X higher than they actually bid. For example: A creature has Resistance 2: Physical A player makes a physical attack against them, the player bidding 3 die. If the creature only bids 2 die to guard, then it technically counts as 4 die, and where they would normally lose the bid, they instead win.

heading: Immunity
text: Creatures with immunity are rare and far between. This is restricted generally for those of high status, myth and legend. It means that any situation specified by a bid that would target them, they automatically win.

heading: Advancement - Merit
text: Every person in the systems starts out somewhere. Your worth is what you make it - and that is measured in merit. Distilled from years of debate and philosophy, merit allows you to carve out aspects of your life and the tools and advantages you take into it. It marks your progression and hard work - your dedication. You will gain and use merit over time - climbing in power and through society. In game the players are recognized for their skill and their contributions - this results in other characters vesting a certain amount of merit in them. When people see your character do things that advance their goals, you complete difficult tasks or the like, others recognize that. It represents your status and your knowledge in game. Therein your character's actions throughout the game will determine your "level." Formally, advancement is gaining different skills and knowledge; there are no levels technically. Your party will earn Merit rather than XP. Merit can be used to advance in skill trees, build out spells, and update stats. Your starting merit will depend on the start you GM chooses for the party. You can find the information in the table below. Starting Merit Table Start Type Merit Maximum Starting Stat Feat Tiers Available Basic 160 4 1, 2 Average 300 6 1, 2, 3 Paragon 500 8 1, 2, 3, 4 Legendary 800 10 1, 2, 3, 4 Players are rewarded merit per session and for completing goals related to various scenes, including combat, socializing, investigations, and exploration. Different scenes can have different amounts of Merit depending on difficulty. Merit must be spent at the end or beginning of a session or during rest and cannot be applied in the middle of some other action - likewise, if the party starts or ends the game during a time-sensitive event, they may not apply their merit. Any other opportunities to apply merit are purely based on GM adjudication. Merit represents time spent learning and training and should be treated as you purposefully taking downtime to grow.

heading: Senexoth Role Feats
text: You are one of many individuals that buzz about the island home of one of the Consecrated families. Whether your role is as small as a fly on the wall, or you’re a direct member of the family - all make an effort on Pthalo to be the best of the best. Pthalo is a prestigious family with more than thirty members - directly serving under the current Queen Mirador. In addition to your background and other feats, you may select of one of the following roles: Not The Chosen One, Servant, Chamberlain, Chancellor, Constable, Jester, Chaplain, Falconer. You cannot overlap with other players and should make an effort to discuss amongst yourselves which role fits who best. Feat Source Description Consecrated Regalia Not The Chosen One You may, or may not be the chosen one. As such, people treat you differently. Opposing enclaves may treat you more poorly, while other civilians may treat you closer to a deity. Behind The Curtains Servant Your station in society is to act as a pillar to the minutiae that others take for granted. Few people notice you, some will refuse to even acknowledge you. Entanglement Chamberlain You spend hours pouring over details, time in the books, keeping schedules and making contacts. Any time you would meet an individual or person with a connection to a governmental position, you can learn one interesting thing about them. To Arms! Chancellor You have a way with words, and knowing certain penal codes. Once a day you can call on any individual using these codes to assist you in a task, whether that is battle or some other task. En Guarde Constable Years spent training as protector and enforcer have leant you many skills the average person doesn’t have. You can take an additional two Combat Expertise in different fighting styles free. I Jest, Good Fellow Jester Any time you personally would have an unsuccessful bid during a social encounter, you can instead play it off as a joke. It will not negatively impact the outcome of the conversation. Cup Bearer Chaplain As an astute member of the Ecclesia Avscein, you have privileged access to history, secrets, and locations that most in society will never see or hear of. Once a day you can invoke the tenants of Avscein to gain access to a location, make appointments, collect an item or other items as appropriate. Companion Falconer You have a special bond with a creature of your choosing, within reason. You can understand each other. You can give them commands, and they will do their best to follow it.

heading: Building a Character
text: This is your story. Whether you embark as a lone expert or with a group of fledgling pilots into the depths of the basin, you play a part in designing your destiny. Your choice is paramount to the system. To begin, you should read through the following sections, making choices and filling in corresponding spots on their character sheets. These can be changed at any point while you’re creating your character; however, changes after the point of starting the game should be discussed with your GM.

heading: Background
text: This determines primarily your outward appearance to others within the world. People and creatures adapt and become the life form that best suits a situation - some backgrounds originated as humans and diverged; others have a deeper connection to the wilds and emerged separately. The following are available to you during your play through.

heading: Names
text: What to call you? Is it what’s on your badge, from a family profession, a locale, or something more personal? Names can be anything you decide - to better fit into the setting, some suggestions are set out below to help decide on naming conventions. Some backgrounds have more unique naming conventions and are broken down below. Every group has some kind of unique first name. Secondary names, middle names, and additional titles usually depend on where you’re from and the setting itself. A basic world dictionary is available at the back of the book for reference for some names.

text: Different groups tend to speak in other languages and by other means. The complete language table is below. At the games' start, you should select two of the languages from the table below. heading: Appearance: Gender, Height, Size, Eye Color, Etc…
text: These should be determined and entered based on preference in the boxes. Please be mindful of your background when selecting certain information. You may reference the background section for helpful information regarding each of these. It is more than possible to fall outside the average bounds for each group; they should merely be used as a guide, not a hard rule set in this particular case.

heading: Size Class
text: There are size classes that are merely represented as numbers; a creature that is a size class 1 takes up 1 five-foot square on a typical grid. Any creature smaller is represented as .75, .5, .25, etc. For larger creatures, a 2 means they take up four squares, 3 means nine squares, and so on. The size class should be listed along with other traits of your background. Typically, characters can move objects smaller than their size class, unless the weight/density is high or the GM makes a specific call. Objects of the player's class size or larger will typically require the player to make a bid.

heading: Vision
text: There are many distinct types of vision, which will be dictated by your background. The most common are denoted with an asterisk; other types are listed for your benefit but may not be available as part of character creation. *Daylight The presence of bright light, either natural or artificial, illuminating an entire area. Creatures with daylight vision typically can see *Lowlight The general lack of bright lights, but some ambient or dim light is present. Creatures that are generally nocturnal usually have low-light vision. *Darkness The complete lack of light: a few creatures have unique vision, which allows them to make out spaces. Echosight You do not have traditional sight, instead relying on sound or vibrations from the environment to determine your surroundings. The world appears to you more as a topographical map. Heat Vision You can see the emitted energy of creatures and the environment around you as visible light, making it easier to navigate at night. Compound You see the world many times over, giving you faster reaction time but poorer distance vision. Aethersight You have a special attunement to various phenomena in the world. You see things that exist on other planes and may be concealed to you. Blindness There are varying degrees of blindness, and how they affect you is a personal choice. Maybe it’s how clear or blurry your surroundings are, or perhaps you only have vision in a certain range or proximity.

heading: Mobility
text: There are multiple ways to get around, and different backgrounds have advantages in different ways. A good swimmer might not be a good climber, and not many can utilize aerial movement without outside help. The primary types of movement are Walk, Swim, Climb, Burrow and Aerial. Your actual speed and reaction time are determined by your Tempo stat and are modified by your background. You will find what types of movements you normally begin with for each background beside your Mobility section followed by a modifier; taking the form of +/-1 or another number, this is what you add to your tempo to determine your speed. Your tempo is never negative or zero; it will always rest at 1. Jumping is determined by your Tempo. It will be equal to half your tempo, rounded down. It cannot be negative and will always rest at 1.

heading: Background Feats
text: Each background will have its own feat(s), which players should add accordingly. These generally only impact play in minor ways. Across the stars you’ll encounter a wealth of people who have their own stories and cultures - adapted to new and wildly varying climates. Below are a selection of different groups that you may see in some of these locations. Human Run-of-the-mill average person. They are largely diverse and adaptable to a number of places and scenarios. Humans by and large are the oldest-known race and continue to extend themselves to all different places and niches. Naming Their last names are typically based on the location, city, neighborhood, or street they grew up at and stay the same even through various life acts. Sometimes prefixes or suffixes will be added if they gain an official title or office. First names widely depend on the planet but are generally wide-ranging and language dependent. Appearance Large variation in human appearances, and various earthen skin tones, including from near black to white. Eye color tends to be varieties of brown, blue, and greens. Size Class .75 - 1 Vision Daylight or Blindness Mobility Walk: +0 Swim: -2 Climb: -3 Background Feats Feat Type Description Specialist Background As a part of your education, you may choose one skill that you gain a 2 bonus die in for any bid. These dice do not incur strain. Adaptive Background You easily acclimate to a wide variety of environments, easier than most. You gain 1 bonus die for any bid that comes from an environmental effect. (Humidity, Heat, Freezing, Etc…) Shimmer A group of specially adapted individuals who primarily grew up in the forest and deep woods. They were among early groups to break off from initial explorers, taking it upon themselves to survey the wild in greater detail than their compatriots. An early divergent group began to develop traits that allowed their better survival. These humanoids are lankier than humans on average but appear to be like them in many other aspects. They have developed many features akin to plants. Naming Their names are derived from their tribal or regional area, usually as a prefix that is unique to them, followed by a suffix that represents their locality. Appearance Large variation in appearances similar to humans, various earthen skin tones including from near black to white with soft green offsets. Their skin can appear slightly translucent in certain light. Eye color tends to be varieties of brown, blue, yellow, and green. They have longer limbs and tend to be taller than humans on average. Their hair is generally various loose vines, which may indicate the region they hail from; some use braiding and hair ornamentation as key parts of their identity. Size Class 1 Vision Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: +0 Swim: -2 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Stoic Background You are more resilient to any effect that would impact you socially. Add 1 bonus die to any social rolls; this die does not incur strain. Hardy Gut Background Your stomach is more accustomed to eating things direct from nature, making you less susceptible to various foodborne illnesses and other related conditions. Giants A group of varied humanoid individuals adapted to the rugged hills and mountains. Their origin is of workers and miners who spent long periods of time away, working and toiling to ensure that their community had access to critical metals and minerals. Most still spend most of their lives in these rocky areas. Growing up, their group's bond becomes more important to them than anything. Naming They tend to go by last name first, which often represents the mountain, hill, or range they belong to. A group is more important than an individual; often many are reluctant to give a first name until they trust someone as if they were a member of their own band. Appearance Largely broader and more muscular than humans on average. They have a range of earthen skin tones, including blues, browns, blacks, greens, and reds. Eye colors tend to be browns, greens, yellows, greys, and reds. They typically keep their heads shaved. Many develop scarring across their bodies, which mimics minerals and natural patterns in the rocks of their homes. Size Class 1 - 2 Vision Vision: Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: +2 Swim: -3 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Faction Pride Background When in the presence of a group that you have positive Sentiment with or share something in common with, you will have additional social leverage with them. Mountain Murmur Background If you listen, you can hear them. Anytime you would be lost, or unsure of how to move forward, you can call on their voices once a day to guide your actions. Rodentfolk Generally composed of groups of squirrels, rats, and mice specifically, these groups don’t have many individual settlements; instead, they tend to be found in large metropolitan areas of humans and shimmer alike. They’ve developed a tongue that uses the common tongue as its base, merely altering word meanings and orders. Naming Primarily inversion and combinations of human or shimmer names. Appearance Shorter than the average human, but taller than their wild counterparts. They are upright, generally with limbs better adapted for bipedal life. Size Class .5 - .75 Vision Vision: Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: +0 Swim: -3 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Survivalist Background You don’t need to cook food, purify water, or even find something particularly edible. You can eat most anything, sleep almost anywhere, and always be refreshed. Alley Cat Background You more readily blend into the shadows. You get 2 bonus dies anytime you bid to become concealed; these dice do not incur strain. Talpids Originally a sect of humanoids who sheltered beneath the earth, the talpids are a group of smaller individuals capable of burrowing beneath the earth. Their hands are typically larger and usually clawed for digging. Many still prefer subterranean abodes and live beneath the surface of the bustle of modern cities. Naming Among the talpids, names are based on skills. Typically, someone's craft or abilities will determine how they are named. Appearance Shorter, stockier, and vaguely mole-like in appearance, they tend to have a wide variety of skin tones similar to that seen in humans, though exceptions have been known to happen. Talpids hands are long and stocky, with three fingers that end in large points like nails accustomed for digging. Their eyes are usually inset and solid black. As well, they are notably hairy. Their noses often tilted upwards, with some having more nostrils than two. Size Class .5 - .75 Vision Lowlight or Echosight Mobility Walk: -2 Swim: -3 Climb: +0 Burrow: +0 Background Feats Feat Type Description Stalwart Background You cannot be made Unsteady, and for any bid that would affect your movement, you have 1 bonus die; this die does not incur strain. Shovel Hands Background You can effectively move through loose soil and earth. You have an additional type of movement called Burrow. Rūn-hem From the deep hills and woods to the vast plains, the Rūn-hem and their kin are a deeply varied group. Their people are known for their storytelling and oral history tradition. It’s said that you can tell where a Rūn-hem is from based on the stories they tell you, their words passed down like heirlooms, generation to generation. Naming Usually they have humanoid first names and take a secondary name, which represents the pantheon their family groups worshiped. These are comprised of the element as a prefix followed by am. Appearance Broad humanoid torsos with the legs of goats, sheep, buffalo, deer, and any number of other hooved creatures of similar nature. Rūn-hem have a humanoid upper torso that is often broader with the legs of a hooved creature and tend to be harrier creatures overall. Their skin tones are similar to those of humans. Their eyes tend to be brighter and occasionally have differently shaped pupils that largely depend on locale. They typically come in greens, browns, yellows, blues, and oranges. Size Class 1 - 2 Vision Daylight Mobility Walk: +1 Swim: -2 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Amiable Background You are well liked, and words spread more easily about your nature. Any sentiment towards you is automatically counted as 2 higher. In addition, any action that would cause you to lose sentiment can be more easily recovered. Peerless Reach Background You can reach high spaces with ease; your jump is twice your tempo, rather than equal to half of it rounded down. Raccoon Unique to cities, these folks have developed clear methods of surviving in high-density population centers. They were first observed in the last century or so in modern cities, having recently begun to take on life and qualities of urban living. Their recent adaptation makes them outsiders in most circles, many sticking to their homes rather than venturing out into the world. As such, the raccoons have a strong family tradition and ties - it’s rare to know a raccoon with a small family or on the outs with them. Naming Relatively new to names, they have come to adopt other humanoids they grew up near, naming conventions rather than develop their own. Appearance They appear as if they are upright raccoons. Their fur can vary from rusty browns to gray and reds. Their eyes are almost always solid black. They are relatively short. Size Class .25 - .5 Vision Lowlight, Darkness Mobility Walk: -1 Swim: -2 Climb: -1 Background Feats Feat Type Description Demiurgic Background You have a knack for how to put things together, even when you're missing pieces. When you make a bid to create or craft something, you can ignore needing to have all the materials to do so, or add 1 bonus die to a bid; this die doesn't count toward strain. Jigsaw Background You are naturally inclined to solving small problems and puzzles. Any time you would encounter something minor in your way, (a locked door, a blockade, a tight space) you miraculously can find a way to solve the problem. Amerem It’s believed that among the old worlds, Amerem were a unique race separate from humans and their ilk that developed as a result of magical interference in their home world. Some myths claim they used to be fairies, but a mistake stripped them of their wings. Nowadays, these creatures work and live side by side with any other in various settings. They have a strong devotion to their trades and have a general pride in their work. Naming Others tend to find their names long and difficult to pronounce - which is why many unfortunately spurn their birth names for shorter nicknames. Often these names will tell the story of their family through short clips and words. Vasins have a rich tradition of oral storytelling. Appearance Short with long ambling limbs, their features tend to look exaggerated in the context of other creatures. They have large, solid-color black eyes and short but pointed ears. Their skin tends to be unusual splashes of multiple color gradients. Some will have green passing into yellow, others reds and blues. Size Class .5 - .75 Vision Lowlight, Darkness Mobility Walk: +0 Swim: -3 Climb: -1 Burrow: -3 Background Feats Feat Type Description Natural Camouflage Background You are less likely to be targeted by others. You cannot be made Conspicuous. Furthermore, you do not need to bid to become concealed. Long Limbs Background Any Melee weapon can be treated as if it was a reach weapon. Melee weapons can be used at 5 ft away. Immersed A group of people who took the water when nowhere else seemed safe. Rumor has it that many originated from sailors lost at sea. Many have the suspicion that the Immersed are so named because one can’t be born as immersed but has to be made. It is rare to see one away from the water; however, they do have the ability to walk on land, albeit in a slower and limited manner. Naming No special conventions are observed; however, some groups might take on the last name based on the water body they grew up in. Appearance Partially humanoid torsos with the lower half of an aquatic creature of different kinds. They tend to have a wider variety of earth-toned skins similar to humans as well as varieties of grays, greens, and blues. Their eyes come in all colors. The degree to which they spend time in land or in water directly affects how human or aquatic they appear. Size Class 1-2 Vision Lowlight Mobility Walk: -2 Swim: +2 Climb: -3 Background Feats Feat Type Description Like Water Background When in any body of water, you are incapable of being affected by any effect or condition that would inhibit your ability to move outside incapacitation or death. Land Legs Background While you can’t be away from water for extended periods, you do have the ability to develop humanoid legs to walk on land. Fairy A group of incredibly small creatures that typically fly. They often migrate, move, and hibernate due to their size. There are few permanent settlements of fairies. Naming Names are typical, though they may be drawn from nature. They rarely take on last names but rather focus on hyper-specific single-word names. Appearance Tiny creatures with mostly humanoid features, their wings vary based on the location of their birth, taking on aspects and colors that help them survive. Size Class .25 Vision Daylight, Lowlight, Darkness Mobility Walk: -3 Swim: -3 Climb: -3 Aerial: +2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Occult Background You are naturally more attuned to magical shifts and changes. You have 1 bonus die for any Stability bids. This die does not incur strain. Miniscule Background You rarely need large quantities of foods or liquids. Bear Deep in the woods, groups of bears have learned to communicate, trade, and build community in the same way as people did but on their own. The bears' society is hierarchical and tends to emphasize inter-community cooperation. They are a magically tuned folk - and highly superstitious. Naming One-word names, and the shorter the better. Appearance Any type of bear, upright is the common appearance of the Bear folk. They tend to have solid black eyes and are slightly more adept and bipedal walking than wild bears. Size Class 1 - 2 Vision Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: +1 Swim: +1 Climb: -3 Background Feats Feat Type Description Mellow Background Any rest you take automatically restores an additional 1D6 Stamina. Stable Background You are more resilient to the alterations at the hands of magic anomalies and cosmic energy. Anytime you’d have to make a stability check, you get 2 bonus dice. These dice do not incur strain. Aerum Their communities and homes are typically out of the way or high above any normal settlement. Some live in high cliffs in clay and stone homes; others live nomadically in tree-top homes built over time. Naming Names are given by elders in the community based on the destiny that they believe the child has in the world. These can be action words or a combination of words to represent a belief or ideal they will carry with them. Appearance Largely humanoid torso that comes in a wide variety of skin tones, from earthen to bright colors. They have arms that double as wings with different feather patterns. Some may have more bird-like features in the face, others more human. Their eyes tend to be solid colors and come in all varieties. Their lower half is that of a bird. Size Class .75 - 1 Vision Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: -2 Climb: -3 Aerial: +2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Airborne Background In any combat situation in an open area, you will have a situational advantage over any opponents. Humming Heart Background Your reaction time is heightened, but you need more food and nutrients to subsist than the average creature. You cannot be surprised. Seeded After a Shimmer dies and passes on, they often leave behind a seed, which can be buried or implanted in a corpse. Some individuals choose the latter to continue living to complete tasks they left unfinished in life. The body can be of any creature or type but usually appears as an overgrown, moss and lichen-covered version of it. Naming Usually take their first name in life with the last name of Novazo. Appearance Seeded share some features with the body they were implanted in. Any skin or tissue is replaced by plant matter of differing types. Size Class .75 - 2 Vision Daylight Mobility Walk: +0 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Undying Background As long as some portion of you continues to exist, you functionally continue to live and can regenerate from even small remains. Verdure Nutrients Background You receive nutrition and hydration through your skin and body from sources like the sun, water, and other things. Undomines A large collective term for a number of amphibious creatures that live in the wetlands. They have largely no formal settlements and tend to be left on their own from birth. Unusually as such, they all pass on some knowledge to their offspring, memories and skills, to each new generation. From birth, it’s a matter of survival; many that make it to maturity move into settlements with other creatures over time. It’s rare for any two Undomines to be in the same area at once. Naming They tend to have a select number of names that they take from the surrounding environments; some take on familial names if they can recall them. Appearance It’s difficult to create a definitive description of these amphibious creatures. Some appear more like frogs, others like salamanders. Generally they have large eyes of any number of colors. Size Class .25 - .75 Vision Daylight, Lowlight Mobility Walk: +0 Swim: +1 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Amphibious Background You are suited to life on land and in the water. You do not need oxygen underwater and can remain submerged indefinitely. Hydration Background You don’t have to expend actions to use potions and liquids, merely touching them is enough. Lizardfolk Making up a small percentage of the population, Lizardfok tend to live away from any large humanoid cities and instead tend to live in subterranean and mountain areas, depending on the variety. They are deeply bonded with their families and carry that loyalty with them across their lifetimes. Naming Generally unnamed until they reach maturity - they are given a name that reflects them as an individual. Up until that point they are named for their colony only. Appearance Small lizard-like humanoids that stand on two legs, they come in various colors and patterns depending on where they grew up. The colors and banding of their scales are an important part of their identity in that way. Their eyes tend to be any variation of color and are slitted. Size Class .25-.75 Vision Darkness, Lowlight Mobility Walk: -1 Swim: -2 Climb: +1 Background Feats Feat Type Description Cold Blooded Background You do not tolerate cold conditions well and tend to slow down in them. When especially warm, you can add 1 to your movement modifiers. Thick-Skinned Background You have a strong outer skin, which allows you to resist oncoming threats better than the average individual. Your guard is always counted as 2 higher. Canis Generally keeping their wooded homes, the Canis are an isolated group that values family lines and is generally unfriendly to outsiders. They are renowned spell crafters and warriors, often acting as advisors and reserve soldiers to any nearby allies. Naming Parts of names are passed down to children from their parents. Each child takes on their own prefix, and the rest of their name is ascribed from part of one of their parents' names. Which parent is usually determined by group tradition. No two children will take the same part of the parents' names; if they have many children, parents occasionally take from grandparents names for their children. Appearance They can appear as large bipedal canines with generally humanoid torsos or as colonies of hyper-aware canines that appear very similar to their wild companions. The variety depends on the pack and history of said pack. Size Class .75 - 2 Vision Darkness, Lowlight Mobility Walk: -1 Swim: -3 Climb: -1 Background Feats Feat Type Description Acute Senses Background You can pick up on the most subtle of sensory clues. For any bid that requires you to track or find an item, you get 2 bonus dice to bid; these dice do not incur strain. Pack Habits Background You thrive in groups or thrive alone; choose one. When you are in your chosen situation, you get an additional 1 bonus die to any bid. This die does not incur strain. Gealán Small creatures, not dissimilar from insects or humans. They appear as tiny winged humanoid creatures with bright patterns on their skin, which glow at night. They often live in small colonies in caves and dark spaces. Some may live in areas that have minimal daylight, as they vastly prefer the night. Naming Appearance Long-limbed human-like creatures with large solid-colored eyes, they have colored markings lacing their body that illuminate at night. Their features are more exaggerated than a fairy, looking more insect-like; some have more insectoid features than others. Size Class .25 - . 5 Vision Darkness, Lowlight, Compound Mobility Walk: -3 Swim: -3 Climb: -3 Aerial: +2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Coven Background In the presence of other Gealán, you do not need to make a bid to cast spells. You more naturally channel in the presence of others. Luminous Pattern Background You can grant a glow to any creature once a day; this takes the form of glowing patterns painted onto their body via magic. This glow dimly illuminates a 10 ft radius. Automaton Automatons are not common by any stretch of the mind and are highly regarded as unique to the ranks of the Ecclesia. Some might still be found in disrepair or in -out settlements. In older settings, objects may be given sentience by powerful casters and can include mundane objects to fully articulated mannequins. Naming Usually named for their originating device, followed by a string of numbers or letters. In the case of a trapped sentience within a device, the automaton may attempt to reclaim its name in life if it can remember it. Appearance Generally humanoid, but they can take on any number of forms accordingly. Size Class .25 - 2 Vision Daylight, Lowlight, Darkness Mobility Walk: +0 Climb: -2 Background Feats Feat Type Description Hydrophobic Background Water, moisture, and its accumulation are the enemy. Over time with enough exposure, parts degrade, rust, or corrode. They will need to be replaced to keep you functioning. Backup Background As long as you are near another living thing, you are essentially without death. You will be transferred to the other entity on the occasion that your first form is destroyed until you are moved again. Restored The undead aren’t seen as something strange or unnatural by most cultures. They are generally repentant people who lived complicated or criminal lives, looking to make up for the problems they had or caused while living. The secrets of undeath are usually held by small groupings who take petitions from various mortals to undertake the rites upon their death. Most undead have only a vague recollection of their past lives. Naming Named the same in life as in death; however, they often share the last name: Morsine, or simply “Without Death” Appearance Take any appearance of another background, and simply be decomposed in any number of states. Most are made with only well-preserved, clean bones, while some traditions use better preserved corpses that are usually only a little more gray. Their eyes tend to take on a glowing cast of color, which can vary. Size Class Variable Vision Lowlight, Darkness Mobility Walk: -1 Swim: -2 Climb: -3 Background Feats Feat Type Description Death’s Shroud Background Treat any injury or condition as 1 magnitude less upon receiving it. Stasis Background You are without the need to eat, breathe, or do most living functions. Scab Over Background Once per day if you have damaged tissue, flesh, or bones, you can replace them with other corpses in a cinch. Remove up to four magnitudes of injuries or conditions.

heading: Feats
text: Feats are at the heart of this game; they determine your knowledge, your abilities, and how you interact with the world around you. You can be actively selecting feats from multiple trees or specialize in one. Some feats provide specific situational advantages; others may help you more generally. It’s up to you to determine who you are. There are seven feat trees to select from. Each feat tree has four tiers. The tiers generally all cost the same, except for a few selections. You may also notice a background section; this contains feats from events in the story, to your selected background. Early feats represent basic training and your personal experience with something. It reflects your style and competence. As you progress through each tree, you gain more abilities, the power to modify rolls, bend rules, and create your own specific style of play. A feat must be unlocked in a lower tier before selecting feats from a higher tier. The Feat Tiers available at character creation are restricted by your Start Type. You may also only have access to certain tiers at the start of character creation, be sure to reference the Starting Merit Table or your GM. It’s important to note that not having a specific feat does not mean you cannot do something, merely that you are unskilled. The GM may then invoke penalties for your actions rather than saying you cannot do something. The trees can be found and browsed on the following pages. The seven trees are Combat, Mobility, Survival, Social, Cognition, Craftsmanship & Magic.

heading: Untrained
text: You might inquire - why do I need this feat? A feat represents a specialization or a boost to an aspect of yourself. Some are more specifically stat-focused, others combat-focused, and some are skills-focused. While it is always possible to attempt a skill without the accompanying knowledge, you will have far more difficulty. Attempting something your character has no training in will result in taking the Untrained penalty during any bid attempting the activity.

heading: Retraining
text: You can retrain a feat, given the appropriate amount of time to do so. Higher level feats should reasonably take more time to retrain. At GM's discretion, you can refund and redistribute merit. This shouldn’t be done on a whim and should represent an important departure or course change in your character’s journey.

heading: Combat
text: While hopefully unnecessary in the day-to-day, some people believe that knowing how to defend yourself is as important as anything else. Combat skills and feats relate to anything that might see you in the line of fire, strategizing and engaging in battle. They improve your abilities with different forms of combat as well as how efficient you are on the battlefield. If the target loses the bid, they lose an action point during their next turn. heading: Mobility
text: Getting around - moving from place to place. Using your hands, feet, and body in different ways to navigate the world. heading: Equipment
text: Players can find possible equipment below and the rules for such items. Keep in mind that there is a difference in inventory and equipped items. Players can generally only have a specific amount of items equipped and active and must spend time to change such items.

heading: The Equipment Tree
text: Each part of the body can only hold one specific type of equipment at a time, unless a feat specifies otherwise. Accessories, on the other hand, have no general limit. (within reason) The sections of the body include: Head, Torso, Arms, Hands, Legs, Feet, Accessories You also have an Over and Under slot for items specifically labeled as to be worn under or over others. Any wearable equipment will list its wear conditions and what slots on the tree it fills. Some may not count, others may count for only one, and a few may count towards multiple slots. You can only have a maximum of 6 Guard altogether from the armor you are wearing, even if it adds to more without special rulings, feats or spells.

heading: Weapons
text: A special note should be made for weapons. They essentially act as an addition to an attack bid. Some may only add 1; others more. All weapons have an effective range, though penalties are typically inflicted for being outside this range unless noted by the GM. Additionally, to use a weapon effectively, you should be trained in said weapon - training comes from the Combat Expertise feat, and specific weapons need special training. Ranged weapons have a maximum range, and an effective range. This means that the weapons do more damage within a certain range, less in maximum range, and even less outside both. Reach weapons are only effective at their reach distance unless noted. Their penalty is similar to ranged weapons; in this way, anything outside their range is at a distinct disadvantage. All weapons are generalized in a way that players are highly encouraged to expand on the weapon they choose; a sword could look any way, same with any other weapon. Name the weapon, select a specific type of sword, etc. The design is in your hands. As you know already, there are three types of damage; most weapons will only do physical damage. heading: Scenes
text: To establish this more thoroughly, there are three types of scenes. Combat, Social, Discovery. Each has their own unique ruleset that outlines various types of events you may encounter through your time in the world. Below each is written about in greater detail.

heading: Combat & Action Points
text: By now the process is the same for all checks, players bid a number of dice against another factor. Players have three action points they can use at base each turn. Each action requires a certain number of points, meaning players need to budget how they are using their turns. Imagine each turn as a five-second slice of time, combat should generally feel fast and end quickly. Below is a table with cost of various actions and things you can do, this is not an exhaustive list, and you can do things outside this with proper communication with your GM and other parties. Action Points Action Notes 1 Preparing A Foci To cast a spell is a two part process, one must first prime the spell foci, then they cast it as a separate action. 1 Cast a spell The actual discharge of power, the action of targeting and releasing a spell. 1 Pulling Out An Object Switching weapons, pulling out potions, etc. 1 Using An Item Generally most simple items, using a salve, applying a bandage. 1 Attacking Most weapons you just need a single action point to use. 1 Loading A Ranged Weapon Whether it’s reloading a gun, or preparing a bow or crossbow. 1 Moving You can move up to your move speed per move action used. 2 Disengage You can move away from an enemy without being attacked. 2 Grab You grab an object or entity. 2 Restrain You hold in place via force or other means an object or other entity. 2 Hide You take time to become concealed from an enemy if possible. 1 Use A Skill Or Feat For basic actions that you have knowledge in, such as recalling information on the fly, learning something in combat, etc. 3 Flee If possible, you can use all of your actions to move completely away from combat and regroup. 1 Speak Saying a short sentence or relaying orders. Attacking Attacks are based on how many dice a player is willing to gamble, some attacks require a minimum and these are denoted by the weapon or feat utilized. Players should read and know their weapons, spells and feats beforehand. Whether an attack hits is directly determined by the other player's guard. They also gamble how many dice they are willing to spend to defend themselves. All creatures and objects have a base guard they will typically use. Guard can be done at any point by anyone, but risks strain. Some feats and equipment can provide the player with bonuses or “passive guard” When you win an attack roll, the combatant will receive injuries or conditions depending on how large the win margin is. Only one die might result in minor injuries or temporary conditions, while higher margins, 3+ result in major and moderate injuries and more ongoing conditions. The player can be descriptive in how they injure the attacked, or the GM can apply the injuries they think appropriate. Threshold (Attack over guard) Injury 1 1 Magnitude of Injury 2 2 Magnitudes of Injury 3 3 Magnitudes of Injury 4+ 1 Magnitude Per Dice Won In A Bid GM Decision Fatal Injury Movement During combat, players can also choose to move a number of ways. A movement is considered any action that would involve your character changing position, retreating, climbing, taking cover, etc. Move To simply move across the battlefield during a scene, you might not need to bid. You will move according to your speed, a number of squares. Hazards, however, might require a bid to avoid. This could be active firing of weapons, spells, or treacherous ground. Flee To escape combat, you will choose to flee using the appropriate amount of action points. Occasionally you will have to bid against the party you are in combat with. In these situations, if you succeed, you successfully flee; failure usually means you are unable to complete the action or meet a complication. This could include tripping or getting attacked as you move away. Composure There may be a scenario where you are knocked off your feet, on the ground, or snagged by some hazard. In this situation, you can choose to get back on your feet or compose yourself for future turns. Unless restrained, you can do this uncontested. While this means you don’t always need to bid, you will have to use an action point. Abilities/Feats/Actions Occasionally, players may choose to instead utilize an ability or special feat during combat. These have their own rules and are described within the text of each feat or ability. They can also do any number of other unorthodox actions, which should be reasonable in the constraint of time of a turn. GMs will adjudicate bids and dice rolls for these scenarios outside the normal scope of combat. A Combat Round For the complete breakdown of combat, here is an example. Process: Phase 1: Combat Order Initiative is determined by either mind/body/soul depending on the scenario. Generally GM will decide unless you have a feat that allows otherwise. Phase 2: Decisions Combat occurs in order of whose scores are best. Each player selects an action from a list of possibilities and describes what they are doing. All combatants will have three action points unless an ability, condition, or feat says otherwise. On your turn you will decide how to use your action points, selecting to attack, move, or any number of other items. Phase 3: Bidding Actions that require precision or skill generally require you to bid. To do so, you will decide how many dice to utilize for your action Multiple 8s: Strain Per 8 & Complications 8: Loose 1 Stamina (Strain) 2-7: Successful Effort 1: Opportunity Phase 4: Outcomes Determine winners and losers for actions and figure out outcomes and injuries appropriately. The next player or entity then takes their turn. Advantage Advantage is a status that is gained through a couple of means depending on the scene type. It represents a number of dice in addition to your own during any bid. These dice do not incur strain. These are generally meant to supplement rolls and do not account for whether players have specific knowledge in a field or task. Combat Advantage During combat, you can gain advantage for a number of reasons. These are outlined here: Surround The Enemy: For each person over one that is in melee range around an enemy during combat, you gain +1 die per person starting at 2. Therefore, 2 people give you +1, 3 people give you +2, and so on. Exceptions: For creatures of larger size classes, the number of people increases for each size class over the largest player combatant required to gain a +1. For one size, that's 3; for two, it's four, and so on. Outnumber the Enemy: If you have overwhelming numbers on the enemy, situationally you may be granted advantage based on GM adjudication. This should be based on the difficulty of the fight. Positional: If you have higher ground, or you have steady footing while your enemy does not, you may count attack bids as +1 higher. This is only added if the user is in the effective range of the weapon. Social Advantage Reputation: generally your reputation is considered the primary counter of advantage during any specific social interaction. Numbers: In some attempts, having higher numbers may afford you a better chance and thus give you a situational advantage at the GM’s discretion. Discovery Advantage Knowledge: If you have unprecedented knowledge of the case, situation, or place based on in game information, you may have an advantage at the GM’s discretion when completing tasks or finding information during an investigation.

heading: Exploration/Discovery
text: When a specific situation requires players to investigate or explore an area or occurrence, a different type of scene may be utilized. Players are on the clock, determined by the scenario and have so much time to discover enough information to form conclusions and inform party decisions. Exploration is composed of a few key components. This includes the goal, discovery track, clues, discovery, and setbacks. The goal is either determined by a third party or the party itself. This is usually to discover the purpose of a device, explore a ruin, find something or someone missing, and more. Similarly to combat, you may have to roll initiative to determine the order of how your actions resolve. GM’s should let you know if this is the case. Furthermore, you will have three action points per turn to determine your path forward. Costs are the same across all scenes. The Discovery Track The discovery track is much like the injury track, except in these scenarios, the players want to fill the track. When filled, the players can make observations and draw conclusions or make a discovery. Players in part are responsible for their discoveries and what they find; the GM is there to affirm what you find. The quality of your discovery is also in part informed by the clues. The track can both act as a timer in some scenarios or a threshold in others to confidently make assertions. Discoveries Discoveries are various aspects of the mystery that helps put the puzzle together. There are a few types of discoveries. Shaky Anything where the logic used to derive may be flawed, there is something instrumentally missing in the information, or the player encountered multiple complications during exploration. Basic A basic fact or piece of information that fills out evidence and asks more questions and points in a direction for discovery. Solid Distinct and solid information based on well-thought-out investigations, which answers more things than it questions. This is usually based on fact and irrefutable in some aspect. Into The Unknown Bidding dice during certain events during an exploration can provide clues, advance the mission, and even reduce the danger inherent in the expedition. Players will interact with items from artifacts, evidence, puzzles, and more to piece together information. The quality of clues/information will depend on the success of various bids, advancing the discovery track. Setbacks These are hazards or events that occur either naturally or as a consequence of player action during a scene. In the same way as complications are primarily narrative, so are these. They can turn certain discoveries into shaky ones, and even affect the entire outcome of an event. If players are up against time, this also means that the discovery track can become filled with shaky evidence and lead to faulty or incomplete conclusions. Completing An Exploration Depending on the threshold of discoveries determined by the GM, when players fill a discovery track, they generally must draw a conclusion or come to the end of their search. Some events may allow more time and, thus, have longer tracks.

heading: Socialization
text: Communicating in all its forms is critical to advancing the narrative and changing the course of any play through. Within certain social interactions players may enter into a specific type of scene, called Socialization. Socialization usually represents players working towards some goal, whether that’s negotiation, interrogation, or building rapport. The various components of a social scene are laid out below. Players' turn order will often be decided based on current sentiment and self-adjudication. You may be asked to utilize action points in certain tense interactions. Influence Track In the same way there is an injury track and a discovery track, this is called the influence track. Players should use these moments to decide how they want to present themselves and their party to the world (or person) and act accordingly. You can do anything from subtly influencing individuals, press them, build rapport, and read their feelings about you. Your interactions during these pressing moments usually fall into one of three categories, negative interactions, neutral interactions, and positive interactions. Certain actions will require specific feats, while others do not. In certain scenarios, you will be asked to bid (roll dice) to determine your success. Often outside parties will already have some opinion of you or your group; it's up to you to guide the discussion and meet your goal. Failures here could lead to decreased opinions, strained relationships, and even fights. Occasionally these failed rolls lead to story complications, which are events that can drive narrative but also make the party think on their feet to find a solution too. Outlook At the outset of any social interaction, both parties have an idea of how they will handle a situation. Some might use force, others might use muscle in intimidation, and others may lie more, and then there might be a few positively receptive individuals. Outlook represents a group's or creature's demeanor at the start of an encounter and can affect the overall tone going into a social scene. Sentiment Player sheets have a contacts section, which shows general opinion towards the player of different societal segments and occasionally important individuals. Sentiment is a simple 1-10 system, with 1 being disdain, hate, and even rivalry, while 10 can be friendship, partners, or even allies. Most people you meet will hold you neutrally until informed otherwise. Sentiment is a longstanding opinion that can be changed by certain social interactions, doing jobs, and sustained contact. Reputation Players also have a reputation, which is a flat bonus added to bids you make towards certain people or entities. Usually this is affected long-term by your party's actions in and around the world. At the start your base reputation will be derived from your mind stat. Poise A stat that represents your ability to navigate social situations holistically; poise is a derived stat that will be used on a number of bids directed at you. While you have sentiment for other parties, Poise essentially represents how easily influenced you are by others.

heading: Spells
text: Spells, or configurations, are a process by which a person, creature, or other entity alters themselves temporarily to channel elements and energy to achieve a certain effect. They can be as complicated or as simple as the caster wants, but do require some work for them to well …work. The first step for any trained spell caster is to build a foci. Within and below are all the pieces anyone would need to build their first spell.

heading: Foci
text: Spells are like weapons or tools, and most people have few spells under their belt. Many spells are unique to their caster; they change and build on them over time. One should keep in mind that they need a device known as a foci to cast properly and avoid unnecessary ameliorations. Think about a radio antenna catching a signal to play a song; a foci catches the energy and power required and channels it into a specific form. Foci’s act as channels that better sort and stabilize magic as they cast; some foci even modulate spells on their own and provide benefits to their wielder. Foci are built around the caster; they are unique to each person and require some investment of self. All spells must have a foci to be cast. Foci are generally any item, artwork, piece, writing, etc., that somehow combine the resonances (components) of a spell to cast. The form they can take is practically endless but keep in mind the setting and the GM discretion. Casting without a foci will result in both a penalty to the user and potential ameliorations. All foci start out as Normal quality and can be improved with time. A normal foci grant no bonus die to casting bids but incurs no penalties. heading: Spell Components
text: All magic is chained together as a series of near-infinite moving pieces; these pieces can be channeled through devices, and a few gifted people can use it directly. These pieces are called spell components for simplicity. When you put enough together, something happens, like words in a sentence. With the appropriate knowledge, a user can utilize the tables below in unique ways to build spells of their own. The more you select, the more expensive the spell. Keep in mind the components merely dictate the spell's rules; you write how that looks, what happens based on constraints, and how it's used. Spell Construction At minimum, for a spell to work, it MUST have a shape, range & an element. This reflects intent in manipulating magic and is the cornerstone of any spell. All spells automatically begin with the following components: Shapeless, Self & Untyped. A spell's "damage" is determined by the specific foci for the spell, as well as any boosts from feats. The focis quality plus your bid determines a spell's strength. Spells have varying casting times that are affected by your skill/feats as well as modulated by duration. Most spells last an instant or ten seconds without modulation of a component. Spells with more components are more difficult to cast without the right training. At base any player can have a spell with 4 (1 target, 1 damage, 1 condition, 1 element = 4) components. For example, if I wanted to build a spell that illuminates another target for ten seconds, I would use my merit to build a spell that has the following components: Range: Aura Shape: Touch 1 Element: Light I could call that spell "illuminate." There is always a chance a spell fails or an opponent blocks or resists a spell. Like a weapon, they can generally be guarded against or straight out avoided. Any additional components can help refine and build on a spell; any spell can be changed over time. Components can be swapped and removed at any point for their merit value, as long as the time is appropriate. Shape This determines the shape of a particular spell upon casting, not the size of said spell. Spells will always have a basic shape and range: Shapeless & Self. Multiple selections can be made in both tables, with magnitude being adjusted thusly. Range modifies all projectiles, not just the first. 10 Unique Special shapes that are unique to a particular spell. Range This section goes over what your spell can affect. Targets can refer to entities or objects in this case. A few can be selected in combination. Targets & Range Cost Type Notes 0 Self Affects only you, the caster. All spells begin at you, the caster, unless the remote component is appended to your spell. 2 Touch X Affects X others that the caster can touch 2 Scale X For each count of X, the spell can be five feet larger. 5 Remote A spell can have an origin point of the caster's choosing in sight. 8 Out Of Sight A spell can have an origin point or target out of player sight. Element To account for resistances and weaknesses, players can choose to type their spells. Multiple elements can be selected for a spell. This represents the body of the spell; these affect what the spell does and how it looks to a degree. It can exclusively be used for minor spells. 4 Social A combination of small magics that influence, change minds, and alter feelings in a room. Duration This represents how long a spell lasts. Typically, spells automatically last about ten seconds, the normal turn length during a scene. However, this can be modulated with components. You do not need to buy each component below the highest time cost you want for a spell; simply decide how long and pay that cost. For example, two turns or twenty seconds cost 4 points, and 2 hours cost 24 points. In most cases, it will be more cost-effective to choose a higher duration if the spell's purpose is to last long periods of time.
